clue.text: Way we must protect lives, aware of urban realities

parts.note: a street is a way or road

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround it, so the word we wraps round the next piece

parts.note: taken as written
lives in the sense of exists, as in 'he is', gives IS

explanation.surface: A guide insists we should look after people's lives while staying alert to the harsh facts of city life.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone streetwise has the shrewd practical knowledge needed to survive in a tough city environment.

clue.text: Some possess a short strip of cloth

indicators.note: some of the letters of the following words are taken, a run within them

explanation.surface: Part of someone's belongings is a short ribbon of fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a band of fabric worn over the shoulder or round the waist.

clue.text: Midshipmen initially employed in adverts

indicators.note: in places the opening letter within the verb for alludes

parts.note: to advert to something is to refer to it

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of employed is used

explanation.surface: Junior naval officers are first employed in advertising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adverts' is the verb advert, to refer, not advertisements. Reefers was old naval slang for midshipmen, who reefed the sails.
explanation.definitionFit: Midshipmen were nicknamed reefers because they worked aloft reefing sails.

clue.text: Giving consideration to receiving guests

definitions.meaning: to entertain an idea is to consider it

explanation.definitionFit: Entertaining a proposal means weighing it up, and entertaining people means hosting them.

clue.text: Pale fellow pinches pound without motive

parts.note: wan means pale

indicators.note: pinching means gripping between the fingers, so the name holds the next letter

parts.note: Tony is a man's name, any fellow
L is the symbol for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A pallid man steals some money for no reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting wantonly means acting gratuitously, without any reason or provocation.

clue.text: Way an air force acquires energy for bombardment

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
RAF is the Royal Air Force
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An air force gains the power to carry out a bombing raid.
explanation.definitionFit: A strafe is an attack with gunfire or bombs from low-flying aircraft.

clue.text: Smart blow caught cheek

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
cheek and lip both mean insolent backchat

explanation.surface: Someone got a sharp slap for being insolent.
explanation.definitionFit: A clip is a quick sharp blow, as in a clip round the ear; smart here means stinging.

clue.text: One's in Irish county, behaving like a job

indicators.note: in places the first piece within the name of the county

parts.note: Louth is a county in the east of Ireland
one is I, and the 's stands for is, so I plus S

explanation.surface: A man from an Irish county is acting like a thug.
explanation.walkthrough: A yob is British slang for a rowdy young hooligan.
explanation.definitionFit: A lout is a rough, uncouth man, so loutish describes the conduct of a hooligan.

clue.text: Person with mates in a number of unions

definitions.text: Person with mates in a number of unions

parts.words: Person with mates in a number of unions
parts.note: reads like a trade unionist with many comrades, but means someone with several spouses through several marriages

explanation.definitionFit: Such a person is married to more than one spouse at the same time.

clue.text: See Western characters disposed to provide inducements

indicators.note: the characters, meaning letters, of the preceding words are disposed, set out in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Go and watch a cowboy film whose heroes are inclined to hand out bribes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Western' looks like a film genre but its letters simply join those of 'See' to make the ten-letter pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweeteners are bribes or incentives offered to win someone over.

clue.text: Prepare port, perhaps, in Scottish island

definitions.meaning: to ... wine such as port is to heat it with spices
an island of the Inner Hebrides off the west coast of Scotland

explanation.surface: Getting the fortified wine ready on a Hebridean isle.
explanation.definitionFit: Mulled wine is heated and spiced, and the same word names an island off Scotland's west coast.

clue.text: Fully functional, like early morning joggers

explanation.definitionFit: A system working smoothly is said to be operating well, and joggers at dawn are literally out of bed and on the move.

clue.text: Stern breed

definitions.meaning: the stern of a ship is its back end
to breed animals is to raise them

explanation.definitionFit: The back part of something is its hindmost end, and raising young is a verb sense of the same word.

clue.text: Issue bound to dog cricket side

indicators.note: to dog someone is to follow close behind, so the leap comes after the cricket side

parts.note: the off side is one half of a cricket field, opposite the leg side
a bound is a leap, a spring

explanation.surface: A matter of a leap tailing a cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' means children here, not a problem or an edition.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue in the legal sense means children or descendants.

clue.text: Note from police officer shot in the arm

parts.note: a super is a superintendent in the British police
a tonic is a boost, a shot in the arm

explanation.surface: A message from a senior policeman who was wounded in the arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot in the arm' reads as an injury but means a boost.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the supertonic is the second degree of the scale, a note.

clue.text: Off balance and not fil enough to lift small weight

indicators.note: lifting a weight means holding it up, so the incapable word carries the weight within it

parts.note: not fit or capable enough is unable
st is the short form of stone, a British unit of weight of 14 pounds

explanation.surface: A weakling wobbles because they are too feeble to raise even a modest weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsteady and liable to topple is off balance.

clue.text: Man put out about the music sung in church

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the next word
put out in the sense of disturbed or disordered, so the letters of man are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man is upset about the hymns sung at a service.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthem is a choral setting of a sacred text performed in services.

clue.text: Curtain in theatre where doctor is involved in dorsal surgery

indicators.note: being involved in something means being caught up inside it, so the doctor goes within

parts.note: dorsal means of the back
op is short for operation

explanation.surface: A surgeon in an operating theatre takes part in an operation on a patient's spine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' suggests an operating theatre but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A backdrop is the painted cloth hung at the rear of a stage.

clue.text: Mission administered by duke after initial hesitation

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation, placed at the start
to run a business is to administer it, so ran

explanation.surface: A task was organised by an aristocrat after he wavered at first.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand is a short trip made to carry out a task, a small mission.

clue.text: Rowdy old American trio unexpectedly appearing first

indicators.note: the jumbled group is placed at the start, ahead of the other pieces
unexpectedly suggests surprise and disorder, so the letters of the three-piece group are mixed

parts.note: US stands for United States, so American

explanation.surface: A boisterous elderly American band of three makes a surprise entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: Riotous means wild and disorderly, much like rowdy.

clue.text: Loudly shows disapproval in military quarters

definitions.meaning: to barrack is to jeer at a speaker or player

explanation.definitionFit: Barracking is noisy jeering, and the same word names the buildings that house soldiers.

clue.text: Anxiety shown when final part of musical performance is changed

indicators.note: the final part of the performance word is altered, swapping its closing letter for another

parts.note: a concert is a musical performance

explanation.surface: Nerves arise when the end of a gig is altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'final part of' says the last letter is the one replaced; the clue does not name the new letter, which the definition supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Concern means worry or anxiety.

clue.text: The question of substance, as distinct from form

definitions.meaning: as in what is the trouble, the issue at hand
the physical stuff or content of something, opposed to its shape or style

explanation.definitionFit: The issue in hand is a sense of the word, as is physical stuff contrasted with form in philosophy.

clue.text: Returned quickly, bearing hot fish

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the phrase for rushing back holds the next letter

parts.note: tore back means hurried back, and torn back is its participle
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: Someone dashed home carrying a hot fish supper.
explanation.definitionFit: The thornback is a ray, a flat fish with spines on its back, found in British waters.

clue.text: There's nobody in this church office

definitions.meaning: an office is a service of daily prayer, here the one said at the ninth hour

explanation.definitionFit: Not any person is the pronoun sense; the daily ninth-hour prayer service, usually spelt with a final S, is the church sense.

clue.text: A lot of the world seeing second half of Disney movie

indicators.note: the latter half of the film title is used, its last four letters

parts.note: Fantasia is Disney's 1940 animated musical film

explanation.surface: Much of the globe is watching the latter part of a cartoon film.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest continent covers a huge share of the earth's land.

clue.text: Small number given go-ahead for retreat

parts.note: no. is the short form of number
an OK is permission, the go-ahead

explanation.surface: A small group was given permission to withdraw.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a secluded corner, a quiet retreat.

clue.text: New dress suit tailored for lasting quality

indicators.note: tailored means cut and made up, so the letters are refashioned

explanation.surface: A freshly made evening suit is built to last.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturdiness is robustness, the quality of being strong enough to endure.

clue.text: The resident patient, for example

parts.note: The Resident Patient is a Sherlock Holmes story, one of the detective's investigations; a patient is also a doctor's example of one

explanation.definitionFit: Each Holmes story is one of the detective's investigations, and doctors also call a patient one.

clue.text: Tendentious publicity from attorney supporting heathen?

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a pagan is a heathen
DA is a District Attorney in the US

explanation.surface: Biased messages issued by a lawyer backing a non-believer.
explanation.definitionFit: Propaganda is slanted information spread to promote a cause.
